Is 1900 in the 19th or 20th century?

1900 belongs to the 19th century. Here’s why the years ending in 00 can be confusing, and how to work out any positive CE year.

In this article
  1. The last year of the 19th century
  2. Think of groups of 100 years
  3. A quick way to work it out
  4. Try the boundary years
Related gameHistory Quiz →

The last year of the 19th century

1900 is in the 19th century. The 20th century began in 1901 and ended in 2000.

Under the conventional AD/CE numbering system, the first century runs from year 1 to year 100. The second starts at 101 and ends at 200. Following that pattern, the 19th century covers 1801–1900.

This is also why the 21st century began in 2001.

Think of groups of 100 years

Imagine putting numbered year cards into boxes that hold 100 cards each. The first box takes 1 through 100. Card 101 goes in the second box.

Each box ends on a multiple of 100. A year such as 1900 finishes its century; 1901 begins the next.

“The 1900s” can mean 1900–1999, so it is not quite the same range as “the 20th century”.

A quick way to work it out

For a positive CE year that does not end in 00, take the hundreds part and add one. For example, 1789 belongs to the 18th century.

If the year ends in 00, keep the hundreds number: 1800 is still in the 18th century.

You can also subtract one from the year, divide by 100, discard the remainder and add one. For 2000: 1999 ÷ 100 gives 19 whole hundreds, then adding one gives 20.

Try the boundary years

Which centuries contain 1600, 1601 and 1999?

Show the answers
  • 1600: 16th century.
  • 1601: 17th century.
  • 1999: 20th century.

The shortcut above is for positive CE years. BCE dates need a different approach to the numbering.
